chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Similar to it, except that he said: 'Saying it three times in the morning and three times in the evening, one will not fear a Satan, nor a ruling authority, nor vitiligo, nor leprosy', and he did not say 'seven times'. Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'And I say it one hundred times'.
ai.seo_question: How many times should one recite the morning and evening suppension for protection according to the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual efficacy of morning and evening adhkar, specifically noting protection from both supernatural threats (Satan) and temporal authorities (rulers), as well as physical ailments like leprosy. The variation in recitation frequency—three times as a standard practice versus Imam al-Rida’s personal devotion of one hundred times—illustrates the flexibility within Shia tradition between prescribed minimums and voluntary supererogatory acts. This practice underscores the concept of divine safeguarding through remembrance, linking physical and spiritual well-being.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it, except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Saying it three times when it is morning, and three times when it is evening, he would neither fear a Satan<sup>la</sup>, nor a ruling authority, nor vitiligo, nor leprosy’, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not say it ‘seven times’. Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> say it one hundred times’.
en.sarwar: 27. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from al- Hassan ibn al-Jahm from abu al-Hassan (a.s.)

a similar Hadith except that the Imam said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘One should say them (expressions in Hadith 25) three times in the morning and three times in the evening and should not then fear any Satan, ruler, leprosy,’ he did not say seven times. Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) has said, ‘I, however, say them one hundred times.’”
